# School facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

For other uses, see School (disambiguation).

"Schooling" redirects here. For the surname, see Schooling (surname).

[![Image 3: First primary school building in Nigeria in Badagry, Nigeria](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/7/7b/First_primary_school_building_in_Nigeria_in_Badagry%2C_Nigeria.jpg/300px-First_primary_school_building_in_Nigeria_in_Badagry%2C_Nigeria.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:First_primary_school_building_in_Nigeria_in_Badagry,_Nigeria.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:First_primary_school_building_in_Nigeria_in_Badagry,_Nigeria.jpg "Enlarge")

 First [primary school](https://kids.kiddle.co/Primary_school "Primary school") in [Nigeria](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nigeria "Nigeria"), built in 1845

[![Image 4: 1st High school of Argos, Greece](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/e/ec/1st_High_school_of_Argos%2C_Greece.jpg/300px-1st_High_school_of_Argos%2C_Greece.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:1st_High_school_of_Argos,_Greece.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:1st_High_school_of_Argos,_Greece.jpg "Enlarge")

 A [high school](https://kids.kiddle.co/High_school "High school") building in [Argos, Greece](https://kids.kiddle.co/Argos,_Peloponnese "Argos, Peloponnese")

A **school** is a place where students go to learn. It's an educational institution designed to help students learn from [teachers](https://kids.kiddle.co/Teacher "Teacher"). Most countries have a system of formal [education](https://kids.kiddle.co/Education "Education"), and sometimes it's even required by law for children to attend. In these systems, students move through different levels of schools. These schools can be run by the government or by private groups.

The names for schools can be different in various countries. But generally, there's [primary school](https://kids.kiddle.co/Primary_school "Primary school") for younger children and [secondary school](https://kids.kiddle.co/Secondary_school "Secondary school") for teenagers. After secondary school, many students go to a university college or [university](https://kids.kiddle.co/University "University") for [higher education](https://kids.kiddle.co/Higher_education "Higher education").

Before primary school, very young children (usually ages 3–5) might go to [Kindergarten](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kindergarten "Kindergarten") or [preschool](https://kids.kiddle.co/Preschool "Preschool"). After secondary school, options include [vocational school](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vocational_school "Vocational school") (for job skills), [college](https://kids.kiddle.co/College "College"), or [seminary](https://kids.kiddle.co/Seminary "Seminary") (for religious studies). Some schools focus on one specific area, like a school for dance or economics. There are also Alternative schools that offer different ways of learning.

Schools not run by the government are called [private schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Private_school "Private school"). They might be needed if government schools don't offer specific types of education. Some private schools are religious, like Christian schools, [madrasas](https://kids.kiddle.co/Madrasa "Madrasa") (Islamic schools), or [yeshivas](https://kids.kiddle.co/Yeshiva "Yeshiva") (Jewish schools). Other private schools might offer a higher standard of education or focus on special achievements. For adults, there are schools for corporate training, military education and training, and [business schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Business_school "Business school").

Some people have concerns about the school system. They might say it doesn't always prepare students well for their future lives. They also suggest that schools sometimes limit [creativity](https://kids.kiddle.co/Creativity "Creativity") by telling students exactly what to do and how. Using things like [grades](https://kids.kiddle.co/Grading_in_education "Grading in education") and [homework](https://kids.kiddle.co/Homework "Homework") might also reduce a child's natural [curiosity](https://kids.kiddle.co/Curiosity "Curiosity") and desire to learn.

In [homeschooling](https://kids.kiddle.co/Homeschooling "Homeschooling") and [distance education](https://kids.kiddle.co/Distance_education "Distance education"), learning happens outside a traditional school building. This can be at home or through a virtual school online. Schools are organized in different ways, like having separate departments or smaller learning groups.

## Contents

*   [What Does "School" Mean?](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#What_Does_.22School.22_Mean.3F)
*   [How Schools Started and Grew](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#How_Schools_Started_and_Grew)

    *   [Schools in Europe](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#Schools_in_Europe)

*   [Who Owns and Runs Schools?](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#Who_Owns_and_Runs_Schools.3F)

    *   [School Buildings and Design](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#School_Buildings_and_Design)
    *   [Schools in Lower-Income Countries](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#Schools_in_Lower-Income_Countries)

*   [Keeping Schools Safe](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#Keeping_Schools_Safe)
*   [Health Services at School](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#Health_Services_at_School)
*   [Learning Online](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#Learning_Online)
*   [Stress in School](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#Stress_in_School)
*   [Rules and Discipline for Students](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#Rules_and_Discipline_for_Students)
*   [See also](https://kids.kiddle.co/School#See_also)

## What Does "School" Mean?

The word _school_ comes from the [Greek](https://kids.kiddle.co/Greek_language "Greek language") word _scholē_. This word originally meant "leisure" or "free time." Later, it came to mean "a group of people who are given lectures" or "a place of learning."

## How Schools Started and Grew

[![Image 5: Plato's Academy mosaic from Pompeii](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/4/48/Plato%27s_Academy_mosaic_from_Pompeii.jpg/300px-Plato%27s_Academy_mosaic_from_Pompeii.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Plato%27s_Academy_mosaic_from_Pompeii.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Plato%27s_Academy_mosaic_from_Pompeii.jpg "Enlarge")

[Plato](https://kids.kiddle.co/Plato "Plato")'s academy, mosaic from Pompeii

The idea of bringing students together in one place to learn has been around for a very long time. Formal schools existed in [ancient Greece](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ancient_Greece "Ancient Greece") (like [Plato's Academy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy "Academy")), [ancient Rome](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome"), [ancient India](https://kids.kiddle.co/History_of_India "History of India") (called Gurukuls), and [ancient China](https://kids.kiddle.co/History_of_China "History of China"). The [Byzantine Empire](https://kids.kiddle.co/Byzantine_Empire "Byzantine Empire") had a strong school system starting in 425 AD. This system helped make sure many citizens, including soldiers, had at least a basic education.

In Western Europe, many cathedral schools were started in the [Early Middle Ages](https://kids.kiddle.co/Early_Middle_Ages "Early Middle Ages"). These schools trained future religious leaders and administrators. Some of the oldest schools still running today include The King's School, Canterbury (started 597 CE). Starting in the 5th century CE, monastic schools also appeared, teaching both religious and everyday subjects.

[![Image 6: BogdanovBelsky UstnySchet](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/a/a7/BogdanovBelsky_UstnySchet.jpg/300px-BogdanovBelsky_UstnySchet.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:BogdanovBelsky_UstnySchet.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:BogdanovBelsky_UstnySchet.jpg "Enlarge")

 Mental calculations. In the school of S. Rachinsky by Nikolay Bogdanov-Belsky. Russia, 1895.

In Europe, universities began in the 12th century. For a long time, the main goal of schools (not universities) was to teach [Latin](https://kids.kiddle.co/Latin "Latin"). This is why some schools were called [grammar schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Grammar_school "Grammar school"). Over time, school lessons grew to include reading and writing in local languages, as well as technical, artistic, scientific, and practical subjects.

Going to school became required in parts of Europe during the 18th century. For example, in [Denmark-Norway](https://kids.kiddle.co/Denmark-Norway "Denmark-Norway"), this started in 1739–1741 to help more people learn to read and write. Many early public schools in the United States were [one-room schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/One-room_school "One-room school"). A single teacher taught all ages of boys and girls in the same room. By the 1920s, these one-room schools started to combine into larger buildings with many classrooms. [School buses](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bus "Bus") then helped students get to these bigger schools.

[Islam](https://kids.kiddle.co/Islam "Islam") also developed its own school system. Learning was very important, so a structured way of teaching was needed. At first, [mosques](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mosque "Mosque") were used for both religious activities and learning. But by the 9th century, the [madrassa](https://kids.kiddle.co/Madrasa "Madrasa") was introduced. This was a school built separately from the mosque, like [al-Qarawiyyin](https://kids.kiddle.co/University_of_al-Qarawiyyin "University of al-Qarawiyyin"), founded in 859 CE. These were some of the first public school systems.

Under the [Ottomans](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire"), cities like [Bursa](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bursa "Bursa") and [Edirne](https://kids.kiddle.co/Edirne "Edirne") became major learning centers. The Ottoman system of Külliye was a complex of buildings that included a mosque, hospital, madrassa, and public kitchens. This made education more available to everyone by offering free meals, healthcare, and sometimes even free places to stay.

## Different Names for Schools Around the World

The word "school" and the names for different education levels can change from country to country.

### Schools in the United Kingdom and Commonwealth Countries

In the United Kingdom, "school" usually means places for learning before university. These include [pre-schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Preschool "Preschool") or [nursery schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Preschool "Preschool"), [primary schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Primary_school "Primary school"), and [secondary schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Secondary_school "Secondary school"). Most schools in the UK are funded by the public and are free to attend. These are called [state schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/State_school "State school"). There are also private schools that charge fees. Some very old and famous private schools are called [public schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Public_school_(United_Kingdom) "Public school (United Kingdom)"), which can be confusing because in North America, a "public school" is usually free and government-funded.

Many countries in the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://kids.kiddle.co/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations"), like Australia, New Zealand, India, and South Africa, use "school" in a similar way for pre-university education.

### Schools in India

[![Image 7: Loyola School](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/f/f4/Loyola_School.jpg/300px-Loyola_School.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Loyola_School.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Loyola_School.jpg "Enlarge")

 Loyola School, Chennai, India – run by the Catholic Diocese of Madras. Christian missionaries helped start modern schools in India.

In ancient India, schools were called Gurukuls. These were traditional Hindu learning centers, often at a teacher's home. Today, schools in India are often called _Vidyashram_, _Vidyalayam_, _Vidya Mandir_, or _Vidya Bhavan_. In southern languages, they might be called _Pallikoodam_. During the Mughal rule, [Madrasahs](https://kids.kiddle.co/Madrasa "Madrasa") were introduced for Muslim children.

Records from the 18th century show that education was common in India, with a school in most villages. Subjects included reading, writing, math, and even science.

[![Image 8: Perumacheri AUP School](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/05/Perumacheri_AUP_School.JPG/300px-Perumacheri_AUP_School.JPG)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Perumacheri_AUP_School.JPG)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Perumacheri_AUP_School.JPG "Enlarge")

 A school building in [Kannur](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kannur "Kannur"), India

When the British ruled India, Christian missionaries started many schools. These schools became popular and set the standard for modern schooling in India. Today, most schools follow a similar model for teaching and subjects.

Schools in India vary greatly, from large campuses with many students and high fees to small schools where children learn under a tree for free. There are different education boards, like the Central Board for Secondary Education (CBSE). Typical subjects include languages, math, science (physics, chemistry, biology), geography, history, and computer science. Students also do activities like sports, music, and drama.

### Schools in Europe

[![Image 9: 1887 Bettannier Der Schwarze Fleck anagoria](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/5/57/1887_Bettannier_Der_Schwarze_Fleck_anagoria.jpg/300px-1887_Bettannier_Der_Schwarze_Fleck_anagoria.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:1887_Bettannier_Der_Schwarze_Fleck_anagoria.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:1887_Bettannier_Der_Schwarze_Fleck_anagoria.jpg "Enlarge")

 Albert Bettannier's 1887 painting _La Tache noire_ shows a child learning about the "lost" province of [Alsace-Lorraine](https://kids.kiddle.co/Alsace-Lorraine "Alsace-Lorraine"). This shows how European schools sometimes taught [Nationalism](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nationalism "Nationalism").

In many parts of Europe, "school" usually refers to [primary education](https://kids.kiddle.co/Primary_school "Primary school") (lasting 4 to 9 years) and [secondary education](https://kids.kiddle.co/Secondary_school "Secondary school"). Secondary schools are often split into _[Gymnasiums](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gymnasium\_(school) "Gymnasium (school)")_ (for academic studies) and [vocational schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vocational_school "Vocational school") (for job training). The term "school" is rarely used for higher education, except for some "upper" or "high" schools (like _Hochschule_ in Germany), which are colleges and universities.

In [Eastern Europe](https://kids.kiddle.co/Eastern_Europe "Eastern Europe"), primary and secondary education are often combined. Schools are classified by "degrees" of education: primary, unfinished secondary, and finished secondary. The first two degrees (eight years) are usually included, and the last one (two years) allows students to go on to vocational or specialized training.

### Schools in North America and the United States

[![Image 10: Farm Security Administration school in Alabama USA 1935](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/3/30/Farm_Security_Administration_school_in_Alabama_USA_1935.gif/300px-Farm_Security_Administration_school_in_Alabama_USA_1935.gif)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Farm_Security_Administration_school_in_Alabama_USA_1935.gif)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Farm_Security_Administration_school_in_Alabama_USA_1935.gif "Enlarge")

 One-room school in 1935, [Alabama](https://kids.kiddle.co/Alabama "Alabama")

In North America, "school" can mean almost any place of learning. This includes [preschool](https://kids.kiddle.co/Preschool "Preschool") (for very young children), [kindergarten](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kindergarten "Kindergarten"), [elementary school](https://kids.kiddle.co/Primary_school "Primary school"), [middle school](https://kids.kiddle.co/Middle_school "Middle school") (or junior high), [high school](https://kids.kiddle.co/High_school "High school"), college, university, and [graduate school](https://kids.kiddle.co/Graduate_school "Graduate school").

In the United States, each state's department of education checks how well schools are doing. Charter schools are public schools that have more freedom from some rules. The terms [grammar school](https://kids.kiddle.co/Grammar_school "Grammar school") and _grade school_ are sometimes used for primary schools. There are also magnet schools, which are tax-funded and offer special programs not found in regular schools.

### Schools in Africa

In West Africa, "school" can also mean "bush" schools, Quranic schools, or apprenticeships. These include both formal and informal learning.

Bush schools are training camps where cultural skills, traditions, and knowledge are passed down. They are separate from the main community, located in forests. Students stay there until their training is done, and visitors are not allowed. Boys and girls attend separate bush schools. Boys learn crafts, fighting, hunting, and community laws. Girls learn domestic skills like cooking, childcare, and how to be a good wife.

[![Image 11: Serrekundamadrassa](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/5/55/Serrekundamadrassa.JPG/300px-Serrekundamadrassa.JPG)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Serrekundamadrassa.JPG)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Serrekundamadrassa.JPG "Enlarge")

 A _[madrasah](https://kids.kiddle.co/Madrasa "Madrasa")_ in the Gambia

Qur'anic schools are the main way to learn about the Quran and the Islamic faith. They also helped with reading and writing during colonial times. Today, they focus on reading, memorizing, and reciting the Quran. Children often go to both state schools and a Qur'anic school.

In Nigeria, "school" includes [daycares](https://kids.kiddle.co/Child_care "Child care"), [nursery schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Preschool "Preschool"), [primary schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Primary_school "Primary school"), [secondary schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Secondary_school "Secondary school"), and universities. Primary and secondary schools can be privately funded (by religious groups or companies) or government-funded (called public schools). Students spend six years in primary school, three years in junior secondary, and three years in senior secondary. The first nine years of schooling are required. Universities can be funded by the government, religious groups, or private organizations.

## Who Owns and Runs Schools?

Many schools are owned or funded by the government. [Private schools](https://kids.kiddle.co/Private_school "Private school") operate independently. Private schools usually get their money from fees paid by families whose children attend. However, some private schools might also get government help, like through School vouchers. Many private schools are connected to a specific religion and are called parochial schools.

**Chance Nickolas Perez** (born November 10, 1997) is an American singer-songwriter, model, and actor. He was part of the boy band, [In Real Life](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/In_Real_Life "In Real Life"), from 2017-2020. He released his debut solo single, "[Can't Trust Summer](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Can%27t_Trust_Summer "Can't Trust Summer")," in 2021. 
Raised in California, Perez has harbored a deep passion for music since he was a child. He was inspired by his father, a musician himself, whom Perez lost when he was only eight years old. He has cited his father to be his greatest inspiration.

## Early life

![Image 5: Perez and his father.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/inreallife/images/b/b6/03D1AB69-2B81-42E0-9898-644C67D42829.jpeg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/148?cb=20180813041445)

Perez and his father.

Perez was born on November 10, 1997, to Shawnee Lanee Perez (née Brown; born September 28, 1969) and Albert Louie Perez Jr. (August 12, 1969-March 18, 2006). He has two sisters: Aspen Kaye Perez (born January 4, 1995) and Presley Kaye Perez (born February 25, 2002). They lived in a small apartment when Chance was growing up, and his father would sing to him and his sister.[[1]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-boyband-1) When he was eight years old, his father died from kidney cancer, and the family faced several difficulties. His mother raised him and his sisters by herself.

Perez attended and graduated from Los Alamitos High School. He admitted he fell asleep during most classes.[[2]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-2) Graduating high school early, he was not able to receive a class ring, so his mother gave him his father's blue class ring.[[1]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-boyband-1)

## Career

### 2014-2016: The Boyband Project and _America's Got Talent_

Perez was in a band from 2014-2015 called [The Boyband Project](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/The_Boyband_Project "The Boyband Project") with four other members: Jordan Perez, Aaron Pierce, Tyler Reardon, and Colton Stevens. He was still in his teens at that time, earning his GED after his sophomore year.[[3]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-3) They covered several songs, including Ed Sheeran's "Give Me Love," posted to YouTube in July 2014, and performed an original song titled "Janet Jackson."[[4]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-4) After the birth of his daughter, Perez departed from the group, and became a certified emergency medical technician to eventually work as a firefighter, in hopes to become financially stable.

Some time in 2016, Perez formed the band, The WVKE, with Jordan Perez and Tyler Reardon. They appeared as contestants in the 11th season of NBC's _America's Got Talent_. In the audition phase, they were buzzed by the judges Howie Mandel and Heidi Klum but received criticism from Simon Cowell, which ultimately led to their elimination.[[5]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-5)

### 2017-2020: In Real Life

In 2017, Perez auditioned for ABC's _[Boy Band](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Boy\_Band "Boy Band")_, a new music competition show produced by Matador Content. Before then, his choir director suggested for him to appear in an episode of the Steve Harvey show as a backup singer. There, he was approached by one of the casting agents of _Boy Band_ and at first declined, but was convinced by his friends and family to participate.[[6]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-iHeartRadio-6)[[7]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-7) He sang Queen's "[Somebody to Love](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Somebody_to_Love "Somebody to Love")" and immediately caught the attention of the three judges, Backstreet Boys' [Nick Carter](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Nick_Carter "Nick Carter"), the Spice Girls' [Emma Bunton](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Emma_Bunton "Emma Bunton") and [Timbaland](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Timbaland "Timbaland"). He, along with Tutton, [Drew Ramos](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Drew_Ramos "Drew Ramos"), [Sergio Calderon](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Sergio_Calderon "Sergio Calderon"), and [Michael Conor](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Conor_Michael_Smith "Conor Michael Smith"), were announced the winners, and signed with [Hollywood Records](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Hollywood_Records "Hollywood Records") as [In Real Life](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/In_Real_Life "In Real Life").

On January 26, 2019, Major Model Management announced over their Instagram account of representing Perez, to which he responded, "So happy to say that I'm being represented by @majormodelsny / Never done this before, but I'm excited for what's to come! Thank you for giving me the opportunity."[[8]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-8)

In January 2020, the band announced an indefinite hiatus, all pursuing solo ventures.

### 2020-present: _Power Rangers Dino Fury_ and music

Since the split of IRL, he started writing and going to the studio, figuring out his musical style as a solo artist. He sent in self-tapes for acting roles, and in October 2020, publicly announced that he was cast as the Black Ranger in the television program, _[Power Rangers Dino Fury](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Power\_Rangers\_Dino\_Fury "Power Rangers Dino Fury")_, which he kept as a secret for months.[[9]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-10) It was his debut role in acting, and filmed in New Zealand. He was featured in Deerock and Wyle's single, "[Bad](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Bad "Bad")," which was released in April 2021. Later that year, his three singles "[Can't Trust Summer](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Can%27t_Trust_Summer "Can't Trust Summer")," "[Stay Golden](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Stay_Golden "Stay Golden")," and "[Cherry](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Cherry "Cherry")" were released.

## Music style and influences

Perez has cited his musical influences to be Michael Jackson, Harry Styles, 1975, Justin Timberlake, Ed Sheeran, and Jon Bellion.[[11]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-11) His father was his greatest inspiration to start singing.[[6]](https://inreallife.fandom.com/wiki/Chance_Perez#cite_note-iHeartRadio-6)

They are known as "Chemma" within the fandom.

The last one is a dove, which he said was for himself, representing positivity.

**Xu Minghao** ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"):徐明浩; [Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):서명호; born November 7, 1997), known professionally as **The8** (디에잇; also stylized as **The 8**), is a Chinese singer and dancer based in South Korea. Managed by [Pledis Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pledis_Entertainment "Pledis Entertainment"), he is a member of the South Korean boy band [Seventeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen_(South_Korean_band) "Seventeen (South Korean band)"), its performance team, and the sub-unit [V8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8_(duo) "V8 (duo)").

In 2018, he had his official solo debut with the release of "Night and Rain" and served as one of the two dance mentors in the Chinese survival show _[Youth With You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth\_With\_You\_(season\_1) "Youth With You (season 1)")_. In 2024, he released his first EP titled _Stardust_.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The8&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

The8 was born in [Haicheng, Liaoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haicheng,_Liaoning "Haicheng, Liaoning"), China[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-1) on November 7, 1997.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-2) He attended Beijing Contemporary Music Academy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The8&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2008–2013: Early actives in China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The8&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2008–2013: Early actives in China")]

The8 began learning [martial arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_arts "Martial arts") at the age of four and later trained in [breaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakdancing "Breakdancing") for five years beginning in elementary school.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-4) He later joined a youth [b-boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-boy "B-boy") crew in China and developed skills in [tumbling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumbling_(sport) "Tumbling (sport)") and [acrobatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acrobatics "Acrobatics"), while also participating in breaking competitions.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-5)

In 2008, The8 appeared on the Chinese program _CCTV Variety Show_. [[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-6) In February 2010, he appeared on [Hunan Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunan_Television "Hunan Television")'s _[Day Day Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day\_Day\_Up "Day Day Up")_ as the leader of the youth breaking crew Dance Power.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-7) During the appearance, the crew performed street dance, and when host [Wang Han](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Han_(host) "Wang Han (host)") asked about his ambition, The8 said that he wanted to become a star.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-8)Audio of the exchange was later sampled in the opening of “Friend”, a track from his 2026 unit album _[V8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8\_(EP) "V8 (EP)")_ with [Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper) "Vernon (rapper)").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-10)

In April 2012, The8 led Dance Power at the sixth BBOY IN SHANGHAI World Breaking Competition, where the crew reached the top eight of the global finals.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-11)

While attending school in Beijing, The8 continued training in breaking and was cast while taking a breaking class.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-12)

### Late 2013–2015: Pledis training and pre-debut

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The8&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Late 2013–2015: Pledis training and pre-debut")]

While attending school in Beijing, The8 was scouted while taking a breaking class and then moved to South Korea to train under [Pledis Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pledis_Entertainment "Pledis Entertainment").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-13) He trained with Pledis for approximately one year and five months before Seventeen's debut.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-14)

In a 2020 retrospective segment from _SEVENTEEN Comeback Show [Heng:garae]_, The8 recalled that while living in China he had watched videos that of the Seventeen trainees from the show and seen them as celebrities before meeting them in South Korea.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-15)

In July 2014, he began appearing with the group's pre-debut trainees during the fifth and final season of _[Seventeen TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen\_TV "Seventeen TV")_, titled _Last Seventeen TV_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-16)

Following Pledis' training process, The8 was confirmed as one of Seventeen's final 13 members in April 2015.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-17) He later appeared in the MBC Music reality series _[Seventeen Project: Debut Big Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen\_Project:\_Debut\_Big\_Plan?action=edit&redlink=1 "Seventeen Project: Debut Big Plan (page does not exist)")_, which followed the group's preparations for debut.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-18)

### 2015–present: Seventeen, solo activities and sub-unit activities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The8&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2015–present: Seventeen, solo activities and sub-unit activities")]

He made his first appearance on _[Seventeen TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen\_TV "Seventeen TV")_ in late 2014.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-19) The8 debuted as a member of the South Korean boy band [Seventeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen_(South_Korean_band) "Seventeen (South Korean band)") with their first extended play (EP) _[17 Carat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17\_Carat "17 Carat")_ on May 29, 2015.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-20) After debuting with Seventeen, The8 also landed a television role in _Real Class - Elementary School_ in 2017.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-21)[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] On December 12, 2017, [Pledis Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pledis_Entertainment "Pledis Entertainment") announced that The8 would be suspending his promotional activities due to a waist injury.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-22) He returned to promotions with the release of Seventeen's special album _[Directors Cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen,\_Age "Teen, Age")_ in February 2018.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-23)

In 2018, The8 participated in the Chinese reality television show _Chao Yin Zhan Ji_ alongside bandmate [Jun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jun_(Chinese_entertainer) "Jun (Chinese entertainer)").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In 2019, he served as one of the two dance coaches (alongside [Jolin Tsai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolin_Tsai "Jolin Tsai")) in the Chinese survival show _[Youth With You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth\_With\_You\_(season\_1) "Youth With You (season 1)")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-25) The8 made his solo debut on June 9, 2019, with the single "Dreams Come True".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-26) On May 4, 2020, he announced the release of a second single, "Falling Down", released four days later.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-27)

On April 8, 2021, The8 announced the release of his third single, "Side by Side". It was released on April 13 in both Chinese and Korean.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-28) On May 4, 2021, The8 released a single called "Mom's Missed Call" along with bandmate Jun, with all proceeds donated to help children in need in China. The single was a part of the Dandelion Philanthropy Music Project for the Chinese Children's Charity Association.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-moms-29) In September 2021, Pledis Entertainment announced that The8, alongside bandmate Jun, would be temporarily taking a break from Seventeen activities in order to work in China for the rest of the year.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-30) The8 and Jun arrived back in South Korea late December that year.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-31)

On March 18, 2022, The8 released the single "Hai Cheng" (海城), which he dedicated to his hometown.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-haicheng-32) On December 4, 2024, The8 released his first EP titled _Stardust_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-33) The Chinese-language EP comprises three songs, including the lead single "Orbit" featuring JinJiBeWater.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-34) On February 2, 2025, The8 began serving as a producer and mentor in the survival show _[Chuang Asia: Season 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuang\_Asia:\_Season\_2 "Chuang Asia: Season 2")_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-35)

On June 29, 2026, The8 and [Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper) "Vernon (rapper)") debuted as [V8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8_(duo) "V8 (duo)"), Seventeen's sixth sub-unit, with their self-titled debut EP _V8_.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-36) The eight-track EP explored electronic and hyperpop-influenced music and included the lead single "singasong", which The8 and Vernon co-composed with [Mechatok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechatok "Mechatok"), as well as The8's solo track "8DM".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8#cite_note-Yonhap-V8-37)

**Xu Minghao** (born November 7, 1997), known as **The8**, is a Chinese singer and dancer. He is famous for being a member of the South Korean boy band [Seventeen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Seventeen_(South_Korean_band) "Seventeen (South Korean band)"). The8 is part of Seventeen's performance team, which focuses on dancing. His music career is managed by Pledis Entertainment.

In 2018, The8 released his first solo song called "Night and Rain." He also worked as a dance mentor on the Chinese TV show _Youth With You_. In 2024, he released his first collection of songs, an EP titled _Stardust_.

## About The8's Early Life

The8 was born in Haicheng, Liaoning, China, on November 7, 1997. He went to the Beijing Contemporary Music Academy to study music.

## The8's Career Journey

### Starting Out in China (2008–2014)

The8 began his career in China at a young age. In 2008, he appeared on a Chinese TV program called _CCTV Variety Show_. He also appeared on another Chinese show, _Day Day Up_, in 2010.

### Joining Seventeen and Solo Work (2015–Present)

The8 first appeared on _Seventeen TV_ in late 2014. He officially joined the South Korean boy band [Seventeen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Seventeen_(South_Korean_band) "Seventeen (South Korean band)") on May 29, 2015. Their first album was called _17 Carat_.

After joining Seventeen, The8 also appeared on the TV show _Real Class - Elementary School_ in 2017. In December 2017, he took a short break from performing due to a waist injury. He returned to activities with Seventeen's special album _Directors Cut_ in February 2018.

In 2018, The8 was on the Chinese reality show _Chao Yin Zhan Ji_ with his bandmate [Jun](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jun_(Chinese_entertainer) "Jun (Chinese entertainer)"). In 2019, he became a dance coach on the Chinese survival show _Youth With You_. He released his first solo song, "Dreams Come True," on June 9, 2019. On May 8, 2020, he released his second solo song, "Falling Down."

On April 13, 2021, The8 released his third solo song, "Side by Side," in both Chinese and Korean. He also released a song called "Mom's Missed Call" with Jun on May 4, 2021. All the money from this song went to help children in China. In September 2021, The8 and Jun took a temporary break from Seventeen to work in China. They returned to South Korea in December of that year.

On March 18, 2022, The8 released "Hai Cheng" (海城), a song dedicated to his hometown. On December 4, 2024, he released his first EP, _Stardust_. This EP has three songs, including "Orbit" which features JinJiBeWater. In February 2025, The8 started working as a producer and mentor on the survival show _Chuang Asia: Season 2_.

**Hansol Vernon Chwe** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):최한솔; born February 18, 1998), known [mononymously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mononymously "Mononymously") as **Vernon** (버논), is a South Korean[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-1) and American[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-2) rapper, singer and songwriter. ## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Hansol Vernon Chwe[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-teenvogue-3) was born at [Tisch Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_Hospital "Tisch Hospital")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-4) in [Kips Bay, Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kips_Bay,_Manhattan "Kips Bay, Manhattan"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") on February 18, 1998,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-5) to a Korean father and an American mother. At the age of five, he moved with his family to [Hongdae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hongdae_(area) "Hongdae (area)"), South Korea. He attended Changcheon Middle School but later opted for homeschooling with his parents after being scouted by Pledis, to focus on his training.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-teenvogue-3)

His stage name comes from his middle name, Vernon, which is also his mother's [maiden name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maiden_name "Maiden name").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-6) Both his parents are artists.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-weverse-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2012–2014: Pre-debut

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2012–2014: Pre-debut")]

Vernon joined [Pledis Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pledis_Entertainment "Pledis Entertainment") in 2012, after being scouted on the street, and received training for the next three years. Beginning in 2013, he participated in _[Seventeen TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen\_TV "Seventeen TV")_, an online reality show that introduced Pledis' trainees and showed potential members of the boy group [Seventeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen_(South_Korean_band) "Seventeen (South Korean band)") before their official debut. The show was broadcast periodically on [Ustream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ustream "Ustream"), where the trainees showed themselves training, singing, creating choreographies, and playing games.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-8) The online show also included participation in concerts, such as Like Seventeen.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-debut-10)

Before his official debut as an idol, Vernon made multiple appearances on South Korean television, including [Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munhwa_Broadcasting_Corporation "Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation")'s _Hello Stranger!_, a program about foreigners in South Korea,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-hs-11) and [Song Eun-i](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_Eun-i "Song Eun-i")'s _Eye to Eye_, where he appeared as an elementary school student who was an expert in dating.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-e2e-12)

### 2015–present: Seventeen, solo activities and sub-unit activities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2015–present: Seventeen, solo activities and sub-unit activities")]

In 2015, Vernon debuted as a member of the South Korean boy group [Seventeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen_(South_Korean_band) "Seventeen (South Korean band)") with the [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play")_[17 Carat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17\_Carat "17 Carat")_ on May 26, on which he contributed to lyrics for four out of the five songs.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-14) Since debuting, Vernon has participated in the songwriting of over 90 songs, making him the Seventeen member with the second-most writing credits after [Woozi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woozi "Woozi").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-komca-15)

In August 2017, Vernon, alongside [Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentagon_(South_Korean_band) "Pentagon (South Korean band)")'s [Kino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kino_(singer) "Kino (singer)"), was introduced as a member of the musical collective M.O.L.A consisting of [15&](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15& "15&")'s [Jamie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Ji-min_(singer,_born_1997) "Park Ji-min (singer, born 1997)"), [Uniq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniq_(band) "Uniq (band)")'s [Woodz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodz "Woodz"), and producer Nathan. Guitarist Hoho later joined the collective.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-16)

In November 2021, Vernon released his first solo track since 2015, titled "Bands Boy", written by himself.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-17) In February 2022, English singer [Charli XCX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charli_XCX "Charli XCX") reached out to Vernon on [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") to collaborate on a remix for "[Beg for You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beg_for_You "Beg for You")". The remix was released February 26, 2022, with a review from _[Nylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nylon\_(magazine) "Nylon (magazine)")'_ s Steffanee Wang describing Vernon's verse as a "grand slam", with "heavy distortion before his silvery falsetto breaks through the digital veil".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-18)

In December 2022 it was announced that Vernon would release the third mixtape for Seventeen's _The Thirteen Tapes_ series: a self-composed and self-written single titled "Black Eye". It was released on December 23, 2022.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-19)

In July 2023, Vernon, alongside bandmate [Joshua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_(American_singer) "Joshua (American singer)"), hosted an [Apple Music 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music_1 "Apple Music 1") summer themed radio show titled _Summer Vacation With Joshua and Vernon of Seventeen._[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-20) He later joined [Blink-182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182 "Blink-182")'s [Mark Hoppus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hoppus "Mark Hoppus")' own Apple Music show _After School Radio_ for episode 169.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-21) In 2024, Vernon was promoted to a regular member of the Korean Music Copyright Association ([KOMCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KOMCA "KOMCA")).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-22) Later that year he was confirmed to have a cameo appearance in [Anderson .Paak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderson_.Paak "Anderson .Paak")'s comedy film _[K-Pops!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-Pops! "K-Pops!")_.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-paak-23)

In June 2026, Vernon and [The8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The8 "The8") debuted as [V8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8_(duo) "V8 (duo)"), Seventeen's sixth sub-unit, with their self-titled debut EP _V8_ on June 29.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-Yonhap-V8-24) The eight-track EP included the lead single "singasong", which Vernon and The8 co-composed with [Mechatok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechatok "Mechatok"), and Vernon's solo track "mia", created in collaboration with electronic musician [KIRARA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirara_(musician) "Kirara (musician)") and Han Jung In.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-Yonhap-V8-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-25)

## Artistry and image

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Artistry and image")]

### Influences and musical style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Influences and musical style")]

Vernon has cited many influences throughout his career. Key [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") influences include American band [Green Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Day "Green Day") and Canadian singer [Avril Lavigne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avril_Lavigne "Avril Lavigne"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-26) which have manifested in songs he has produced, such as Seventeen's "2 Minus 1" and his own "Black Eye".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-rollingstone-27) He has also indicated interest in [hyperpop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperpop "Hyperpop") and [experimental pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_pop "Experimental pop"), many times crediting British singer [Charli XCX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charli_XCX "Charli XCX") as an influence,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-28)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-weverse-7) specifically for Seventeen's track "Gam3 Bo1".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-teenvogue-3) He has also indicated he is a fan of [Bladee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bladee "Bladee"), [100 gecs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/100_gecs "100 gecs"), and [The Kid Laroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kid_Laroi "The Kid Laroi").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-weverse-7)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-29)

### Fashion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Fashion")]

In 2023, Vernon was announced as the first global ambassador for French fashion house [Kenzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenzo_(brand) "Kenzo (brand)").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-30) Since the announcement, Vernon has attended multiple shows for the brand at [Paris Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Fashion_Week "Paris Fashion Week")[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-31) and was the face of the brand's FW23 campaign.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-32)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Vernon holds dual South Korean and American citizenship.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-Newsis-2026-33)

### Military service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vernon_(rapper)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Military service")]

On August 20, 2026, Vernon began his [mandatory military service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_South_Korea "Conscription in South Korea"), entering a training center to receive basic military training, after which he will serve as a [social service worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_service_personnel "Social service personnel"). His service is scheduled to conclude on May 19, 2028.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_(rapper)#cite_note-Newsis-2026-33)
